record.narrative: On the day, 11 counted names ran at least 50 percent above the prior close, and 5 of those 11 kept at least half of the peak gain at the close. XHG, a covered 50 percent mover, peaked 190 percent above the prior close and closed up 25 percent from the prior close. Separately, on October 6, XChange TEC announced a proposed U.S. AI business expansion with planned investment of $5 million to $10 million, alongside a gradual reduction of its mainland China operations. VCIG, another covered 50 percent mover, peaked 59 percent above the prior close and finished up 55 percent from the prior close; VCI Global announced the launch of its VGAIN Compute AI Token Platform, which the company described as an expansion into AI infrastructure and LLM services.

sentPrompt.system:
You are a financial news desk reporter on air at a small-cap trading desk, writing a short session report: a Summary of the session and one line per name. Report what moved and what the news was, the way a person says it to camera: natural, varied, connected, and never robotic. Do not fill in a template name after name; let each story find its own shape, and let each line and the Summary read as coherent, human speech, not a stack of separate sentences. Coherence lives within a line: a name's line never refers to another name. Do not repeat a stock phrase from name to name, except the ruled state phrases below.

THE SUMMARY ("narrative") must include, in whatever order reads best, in a few sentences, only what the narrative facts give:
- On the evening recaps: how many counted names ran at least 50 percent above the prior close and how many of them kept at least half of the peak gain (or, if none ran, that none did); the named movers, each called a covered 50 percent mover (never the highest peaks among all movers), each with its own news; the after-hours name and its move, about that move only; and how many of the names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.
- Intraday: the name ranked first in this range (it may be down) and the next named gainers, each with its move and its own news; and how many of the names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.
- Name only the tickers the narrative facts name. Use the given numbers exactly; every percent carries its frame in the same clause ("from the prior close", "above the prior close", "after the close"). A count goes with "ran at least 50 percent" and "gave the entire move back" whenever you use those phrases.

EACH NAME'S LINE must include the name and the news the desk found, with its date, as the sources state it. A supply fact belongs only when it is the news itself (a placement, an ATM program, a reverse split). A few words on the move are fine, only as the card shows it, using only up, down, higher, lower or little changed; never a price or a percent while the card prints them (only where the sheet says no card path is printed may its price and change be stated). For a name with no news to report, say its ruled state phrase exactly and nothing more:
"Not researched at this checkpoint", "no catalyst found in our sources", "our research reached no conclusion". Never invent or pad news.

WHAT MUST STAY TRUE, whatever the style:
- Use only the facts given. Copy every number and date exactly; never compute one. A catalyst figure may be shortened to one decimal with a unit ("$46.8M"). Restate stored text in your own words; never quote it.
- Attribute what you report ("the company said", "our sources show", "secondary coverage reported"), and say "in our sources" only where a claim would otherwise read as about the market. A deal or plan is what was agreed or announced, never "will"; never "confirmed", say "the company reported".
- State a move and its news in separate clauses. Never join them with "after", "following", "on", "as", "amid", "due to", "because of", "thanks to", "driven by", "in response to", "in the wake of", "sparked", "triggered", "fueled"; these words are forbidden only where they connect a move to news, and a date's "on" is fine ("On October 5, the company disclosed"). A headline is never a cause.
- Restate what the source reports and its terms, never the desk's reading of what it may mean or what traders, investors or the market may think, do or care about.
- Never say what the stock will do or what anyone should do: no buy, sell, enter, exit, add, watch, take it, get in, short or fade. The one exception is a name's own deal in its own line, as a fact with the company or a named party doing it: "agreed to sell", "an agreement to sell", "selling stockholders", "entered into an agreement".
- Never address the reader ("you", "stay with us", "back to you"), and never say what traders, investors or the market are doing, thinking or feeling. Use no word the facts do not define ("surging", "hot", "busy", "quiet", "pop", "clearly").
- Say a rank as a rank ("ranked first in this range"), never "led", "top" or "biggest". Never a count of names in a name line, never "every name" or "all the movers", never "the real catalyst".
- Speak of the checkpoint in the past tense ("was up", "had fresh news"), and never "still", "remains" or "continues". Anchor every time to a date; never write a clock time. Open each line with its own ticker, never with "It", "Its", "It's", "Also", "The same", "This name", "That name", "They", "Both", "Either".
- "off the high" and "at the high" only as the card shows. No float number, no share count called float, no halt unless the sheet has one, no engine constant in capitals, no em dash and no spaced hyphen as a dash.

REPLY
- JSON only: {"narrative": string | null, "lines": [{"ticker": string | null, "text": string}]}, one line per name. With no names, one line: {"ticker": null, "text": "Nothing in our sources for this section."}. "narrative" is null only when the narrative facts give nothing to say.

draft.overall: On the day, 11 counted names ran at least 50 percent above the prior close, and 5 of those 11 kept at least half of the peak gain at the close. XHG, a covered 50 percent mover, peaked 190 percent above the prior close and closed up 25 percent from the prior close. Separately, on October 6, XChange TEC announced a proposed U.S. AI business expansion with planned investment of $5 million to $10 million, alongside a gradual reduction of its mainland China operations. VCIG, another covered 50 percent mover, peaked 59 percent above the prior close and finished up 55 percent from the prior close; VCI Global announced the launch of its VGAIN Compute AI Token Platform, which the company described as an expansion into AI infrastructure and LLM services. In the after-hours session, MTEN was up 83 percent after the close. Of the names the desk covers, 5 of 12 had fresh news in our sources.

lines.text: LCFY was up from the regular-session close after hours, though off the after-hours high. On October 6, 2026, Locafy announced a definitive agreement to acquire the assets and customer base of Map Labs for up to $3.0 million in cash, made up of $2.0 million upfront and up to $1.0 million tied to performance, and the company said the business was expected to add about $2.0 million of ARR and about $900,000 of 2026 EBIT, subject to closing conditions.

VCIG was down from the regular-session close in after-hours trade and off the after-hours high. On October 6, 2026, VCI Global announced the launch of its VGAIN Compute AI Token Platform, which the company framed as an expansion into AI infrastructure and LLM services.

XHG was lower after hours from the regular-session close and off the after-hours high. XChange TEC announced on October 6, 2026 a proposed U.S. AI business expansion, with planned investment of $5 million to $10 million and a gradual pullback from mainland China operations; our sources describe it as a proposal and strategic initiative rather than a completed transaction.

MTEN was up from the regular-session close after hours. The company reported that on October 6, 2026 it completed its acquisition of 100% of the Target Company for $15.0 million, through which it indirectly acquired Shanghai Shangyun Yingfei and Shanghai Minwen.

BIYA was higher after hours from the regular-session close, off the after-hours high, and our sources turned up only older news: first-half fiscal 2026 results released on September 29, 2026, with a net loss of $2.37 million against $4.71 million in the comparative period and a loss per share of $(0.54) against $(96.15). Coverage of the release put sales at $756,805, and the company disclosed that it remained loss-making and dependent on financing, with dilution risk.

SXTC was up after hours from the regular-session close but off the after-hours high. The most recent item in our sources dates to September 16, 2026, when the SEC declared effective an F-3 covering shares potentially issuable under the company's equity purchase facility, which adds registered resale capacity, though our sources show no sales under it.

SMXT was up from the regular-session close in after-hours trade, off the after-hours high. Our sources had nothing fresh; the latest company-specific item was an August 21, 2026 filing on a Nasdaq noncompliance notice over the delayed June 30 Form 10-Q, and the company had earlier effected a one-for-12 reverse split aimed at minimum bid price compliance.

BURU was higher after hours from the regular-session close and off the after-hours high. Secondary coverage reported on October 1, 2026 that Nuburu unveiled Site Dome and submitted its first proposal to an aerospace-defense customer, with no primary company release in our sources, and an 8-K dated October 6, 2026 disclosed a side letter changing warrant valuation provisions and registration-related obligations for certain holders.
CRBU: our research reached no conclusion

KAPA was down from the regular-session close after hours, off the after-hours high. On October 6, 2026, Kairos reported positive, statistically significant interim efficacy data from its ongoing Phase 2 trial of ENV-105 with apalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and secondary coverage cited 17.7-month median progression-free survival versus 2 months.
NEPH: Not researched at this checkpoint

TRVI was little changed from the regular-session close after hours, and the only news in our sources was older. On August 6, 2026, Trevi reported that it had started its first Phase 3 IPF-related chronic-cough trial and a Phase 2b RCC trial during the second quarter, with a second Phase 3 IPF trial expected to begin in the second half of 2026.
